input: arr is a mutable list/array of 1 through 10000 integers in [1,10000], with duplicates permitted. Collections are ordinary finite dense arrays/lists, not subclasses, proxies, sparse/accessor-backed collections. Strings are ordinary/primitive strings. Every collection length and computed allocation size fits [0,4294967295], with padded sizes explicitly included. No concurrent mutation or built-in monkey-patching is allowed. Preconditions are not runtime-checked, and allocation/resource capacity or completion is not guaranteed by declared bounds. JavaScript integer inputs are primitive safe-integer Number, excluding negative zero, NaN, infinities, fractions and BigInt.
return: The original arr object, containing the lexicographically largest strictly smaller permutation reachable by exactly one swap, or the unchanged original arr when no smaller permutation can be reached.
mutation_aliasing: At most two entries of caller-owned arr are exchanged, using unequal values when a smaller result exists; all aliases observe that exchange. Length and object identity are preserved, and the return aliases arr. No writes occur in the no-smaller-result branch. The Solution instance retains no state.
numeric: Indices stay in [-1,n-1]. The rightmost descent preserves the longest possible prefix. Its nondecreasing suffix supplies the largest smaller value; its leftmost equal occurrence leaves the largest suffix after swapping. All integer inputs/intermediates remain within [-9007199254740991,9007199254740991]; no bitwise coercion is used.
complexity: O(n) time and O(1) auxiliary storage. The constant-size swap temporary is included. Bounds include ordinary built-in operations/allocations and assume bounded-word arithmetic, constant-time indexing, amortized append/pop and any explicitly stated hash/sort behavior.
